summary:
Our project is a decision-based project, which is to provide the farmer with the best crop rotation for the next seasons and connects the NASA data observations to ground-level agricultural decision-making.
I developed, with my team, a machine learning model to provide the farmer with the best crop rotation.

Because climate and crops vary by continent, and because climate differs between the Northern and Southern Hemispheres, we created 2 models for every country and trained them using NASA-provided data using his orbits. Despite the difference in climate and crops, I took 2 nations for every continent. Our project is a decision-based project, which is to provide the farmer with the best crop rotation for the next seasons.

We addressed the challenge by engineering a crop rotation engine that relies 100% on real-time and historical satellite data rather than scarce historical yield datasets. We built an automated data pipeline that extracts precise environmental metrics—as my features to train the model, specifically NASA SMAP Level 4 for surface and root-zone soil moisture, GPM for precipitation, and MODIS for temperature profiles. We then algorithmically merged this space-derived data with the FAO EcoCrop database
details:
My project bridges NASA data observations with real ground architecture; it consists of multi-machine learning models trained on provided NASA data, it provides the farmer with the best rotation crop for the next seasons to prevent soil harm, and it prevents the impact of climate change.

I chose it to be multi-models because of the difference in crops, climate, and soil types and characteristics. 12 models for all over the world, 2 for every continent. I chose two notions in the same continent, one in the north and one in the south.

When the farmer opens the website, he will choose the location of his farm. Based on his farm's location, we select the model and retrieve the soil properties and climate from NASA data using the latitude and longitude he provided when he chose his farm's location. I get the soil properties, then push them into the model, and then the model produces the best rotation.

The benefits and impact of our project are regenerative agriculture, soil healing, climate resilience, risk mitigation, and global scalability.

Regenerative Agriculture & Soil Healing:

We use feature engineering skills to create the soil impact score, which ensures that the soil is never depleted by strategy. Alternating the heavy feeders like corn with nitrogen fixers like soybeans makes the engine restore soil fertility

Climate Resilience & Risk Mitigation:

Traditional planting calendars are obsolete due to climate change. By using up-to-date NASA SMAP and GPM data, our engine adapts to shifting rainfall and temperature patterns, protecting farmers from unexpected droughts or crop failures.
global scalability:

The project is not limited to one region; we have already used multi-models for multiple climates and soils using global NASA satellite data and FAO standards. We successfully tested it across 12 different countries spanning all continents and both hemispheres.

We used Python and React.js, libraries like pandas.

Our project shows creativity in using multiple models after observing the different factors in every continent.

My team considers the different factors between continents.
